chunks: Abū Muḥammad has become a stranger in this place!
By Allāh, I did not like that the Quraysh should lie killed under the stars!
I have avenged myself with the descendants of ‘Abd Manāf, but the chief persons of Banū Jumaḥ have escaped me,
They had stretched their necks towards a matter for which they were not suited, and therefore their necks were broken before they reached the goal.

key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ: Abu Muhammad (a title for Talhah ibn Ubaid Allah)
key_terms.بَنُو جُمَحَ: Banu Jumah (the clan of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam)
key_terms.بَنُو عَبْدِ مَنَافَ: Banu Abd Manaf (the clan of Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.قُرَيْشٌ: Quraysh (the tribe of the Prophet Muhammad)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the Quraysh killing each other in the Battle of the Camel?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) reflects on the tragedy of the Quraysh killing each other, expressing that his personal vendetta against the Banu Abd Manaf (his own clan) was fulfilled, yet the leaders of Banu Jumah escaped his grasp. This highlights the internal tribal fractures within the early Muslim community, where personal grievances and clan loyalties complicated the broader political and religious unity. The narration underscores the sorrow of a leader witnessing his own people divided, emphasizing the cost of civil strife even among the elite of Quraysh.
